Ratings are kept if their daily price is strictly above that mean. The output is one row with three values: the mean of the kept ratings' average replacement costs, the mean of their daily prices, and the mean of (daily price − cross-rating average) over them.
The same as 1, but the cross-rating average is weighted by film count. That is the overall average of daily price across all films, not the mean of the 5 ratings' values.

queries:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS dp, AVG(replacement_cost) AS rc
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
),
m AS (
  SELECT AVG(dp) AS mdp FROM r
)
SELECT AVG(r.rc), AVG(r.dp), AVG(r.dp - m.mdp)
FROM r, m
WHERE r.dp > m.mdp;
SELECT AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_daily_price FROM film;
SELECT rating
FROM film
GROUP BY rating
HAVING AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) >= (SELECT AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) FROM film);
SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate) / AVG(rental_duration) AS avg_daily_price FROM film GROUP BY rating
SELECT AVG(length) FROM film WHERE <kept-rating condition>;
SELECT f.rating,
       AVG(f.rental_rate) AS avg_rental_rate,
       AVG(f.length) AS avg_length,
       (SELECT AVG(f2.replacement_cost)
        FROM inventory i2
        JOIN film f2 ON f2.film_id = i2.film_id
        WHERE f2.rating = f.rating) AS avg_replacement_cost
FROM film f
WHERE f.film_id IN (SELECT film_id FROM inventory)
GROUP BY f.rating;
